text:
Arsenal continue to be a sharp thorn in the side of the European champions, Barcelona, digging deep to hold on for a draw. Frida Maanum put the Gunners ahead despite a hugely dominant performance from Barcelona, but Caroline Graham Hansen’s equaliser ensured the spoils would be shared.
The last time these two teams met, Arsenal were lifting aloft the Champions League trophy at Barcelona’s expense after the most perfect of defensive performances and a Stina Blackstenius goal in Lisbon in 2025. It was a far less perfect defensive performance this time, but Arsenal showed guts against the team that retook their crown last season and showed they can play ugly when needed.
There was one change to the team that earned a 2-1 win against Liverpool on Sunday, but it was a significant one. Olivia Smith was replaced by Frida Maanum and the Norwegian slotted into the No 10 role with Alessia Russo, who has scored 12 goals in nine games for club and country, moving into the centre-forward position. Russo’s position has been a constant talking point during Arsenal’s struggles, but her exploits have shown where she plays does not really matter.
It was play on the left that provoked the shock first-half goal here that temporarily silenced the crowd. The 27-year-old beat two and worked the ball to Maanum. Barcelona got the ball away, but Russo was there again and delivered a perfect cross across the face of goal for Caitlin Foord. The Australian forced a close-range save from Cata Coll, but Maanum was there to power in the loose ball.
The pocket of travelling fans behind plexiglass in the upper tier were jubilant. About 1,000 had travelled despite the late switch of the match to Thursday due to a 24-hour general strike in Spain on Wednesday.
It was a goal decidedly against the run of play, but Barcelona struggled to capitalise on their dominance in the first half, despite some shaky moments at the back from the visitors. Ewa Pajor and Caroline Graham Hansen were particularly threatening as Barcelona targeted Arsenal’s left, made up of the less experienced Taylor Hinds and Lisa Baum.
The scoreline at the break was a little unfathomable based on the run of play and the domestic fortunes of both sides. While Arsenal languish in sixth in the WSL, 12 points behind the league leaders, Manchester City, Barcelona have won nine of their 10 games in Liga F, having scored 41 goals and conceded five and have a five point lead over their nearest rivals, Real Madrid.
Arsenal’s gameplan felt familiar, it was as if they had studied the blueprint religiously followed by teams that have sat back in a low block and frustrated them week-in week-out in the WSL this season.
Pere Romeu had made three changes to the team that earned a 5-1 win over Real Madrid on Sunday and the surprise was that three-time Ballon d’Or winner Aitana Bonmatí was relegated to the bench. It was her arrival, though, shortly before the hour mark that elevated Barcelona’s threat, causing Arsenal’s defending to look even more calamitous at times, and lifted the mood in a frustrated stadium.
They were soon level, Esmee Brugts found an unmarked Graham Hansen on the right and she cut inside and swept in past Misa Rodríguez. It was way too easy for the Norway forward, who was unfazed by the arrival of two defenders before she struck.
It was no surprise that a run-ragged Baum and Hinds were removed soon after, with former Barcelona player Ona Batlle and Smith, Arsenal’s record signing, replacing them.
Arsenal were better after the goal and the changes, occasionally breaking free of their prison of a final third. At the end they were clinging on, but cling on they did, to take a big point away from home and demonstrate they can work to a different gameplan when required.
